title: Dedicated capacity fair-share & surge governance playbook
creator: Arielle Kim
description:
Problem: Customers with reserved Dedicated pools occasionally experience noisy-neighbor surges (scheduled jobs, batch traffic, or misconfigured burst clients) that degrade latency for other tenants and trigger buffer autoscale actions. Current autoscale behavior is reactive; we lack a unified governance layer that enforces fair-share during surges, maps billing to capacity choices, and provides predictable rollback behaviors for critical customers.

Goal: Create a playbook and implement the first-phase governance primitives that let operators and the control plane: 1) enforce soft and hard fair-share policies within a dedicated pool, 2) apply surge prioritization rules (reserve, fair-share, preemptible), 3) produce billing-adjusted surge pricing signals and customer notifications, and 4) provide safe rollout and rollback controls for pilot customers.

Scope (MVP):
- Governance policy schema: priority tiers, token buckets, preemption thresholds, soft-fair windows, and emergency pinning.
- Runtime primitives: request tagging, per-tenant queueing, preemption hooks, and immediate fallback to lower-cost model variants.
- Console UX: policy editor, per-pool policy assignment, conflict visibility, and surge timeline view.
- Billing & communication: surge-unit accounting, automated emails for sustained surges, and billing preview calculations for pilot customers.
- Pilot: three mid-market customers with different commitment profiles (100%, 50%, 0% reserved) running for 6 weeks with close SLO monitoring.
acceptance_criteria: Governance policy schema implemented and validated in staging
Per-tenant fair-share enforced in canary pool with no >5% increase in 95p latency for non-triggering tenants
Console shows active policies and a 24h surge timeline for the pilot pools
Billing preview accurately estimates surge charges within ±10% for pilot scenarios
Rollback and emergency-pin flow tested with documented runbook and two engineers able to revert in <10 minutes
milestones: Week 1: Design policy schema + operator runbook
Week 3: Runtime tagging + per-tenant queue prototype in staging
Week 5: Console policy editor alpha + billing preview integration
Week 8: Pilot canary with 3 customers; monitor SLOs
Week 12: Post-pilot retro and decision: extend, iterate, or rollback
risks: Complexity in preemption can cause silent request failures if not instrumented
Billing estimators may under/over-index on model variant fallback patterns
Operator errors (mis-applied policy) could unintentionally throttle high-value customers
Telemetry volume during surges may increase costs and lead to missing signals if dashboards aren't aggregated
